newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SHEARER PENALTY HELPS SINK FORMER CLUB BLACKBURN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHEARER PENALTY HELPS SINK FORMER CLUB BLACKBURN.

text.p: Alan Shearer scored from a controversial penalty against his former club Blackburn on Saturday to set Newcastle on their way to a 2-1 victory which took them to third in the premier league.

The England striker, who left Blackburn last month for a world-record 15 million pounds ($23.3 million), smashed home his spot kick after Scotland defender Colin Hendry was harshly adjudged to have handled in the area on the stroke of halftime.

Les Ferdinand added his fourth goal in three league games after the break, and although Blackburn pulled one back through Shearer's former striking partner Chris Sutton five minutes from time, Kevin Keegan's side held on to win.
Newcastle are now level on points with top-of-the-table Manchester United, who came from behind to beat Nottingham Forest 4-1, and early pacesetters Sheffield Wednesday.

Wednesday can leapfrog back to the top on Monday when they face Arsenal, reeling from the resignation on Friday of caretaker manager Stewart Houston, and captain Tony Adams' admission on Saturday he is an alcoholic.
High-flyers Chelsea and Aston Villa meet each other on Sunday.
Shearer was unsentimental about a result which pushes 1995 champions Blackburn to the bottom of the league table with just one point from six games.

Asked about the penalty decision, which brought a storm of protests from his former colleagues, he said: "No-one intends to handle the ball in the box, but it's hit (Hendry's) hand, and in my opinion if it hits your hand in the area it's a penalty."
Goalkeeper Tim Flowers, who has played with Shearer at Southampton, Blackburn and for England, guessed correctly, diving to his right, and almost saved the kick.
"Tim phoned me last night and told me he'd know which way to go if there was a penalty," Shearer said with a smile. "He did, but fortunately he didn't reach it."
Leeds defender Andy Couzens gave George Graham the perfect welcome back to soccer after 18 months in the wilderness, scoring in the opening minute against bottom-side Coventry.
Graham took over as manager of the Elland Road club this week -- his first job since sacked as boss of London giants Arsenal in early 1995 for accepting illegal payments from transfer deals.

But Graham's return was soured in the second half as Coventry, bottom of the table before start of play, equalised through John Salako, and then scored the winner through former Leeds favourite Noel Whelan.
There was a touch of deja vu for Frenchman Eric Cantona at Old Trafford, where defending champions United recorded their first home win of the season.
For the second consecutive Saturday the midfielder scored United's fourth goal in the final minute of the match, and for the second consecutive Saturday he had a penalty to take.
That's where the similarities ended though.

Last week at Leeds, Cantona missed his spot kick before scoring from open play. This week, against Nottingham Forest, he found the net with a fierce drive from outside the box, then rounded off the win from the spot with seconds remaining.
Forest took an early lead through Norwegian international Alf-Inge Haaland, but saw it blown away by goals from Haaland's compatriot Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Ryan Giggs, and Cantona.
The result came as welcome relief for United, who scrambled 2-2 draws in their previous two home games, and lost 1-0 to Italy's Juventus in the European Champions' League in midweek.
United have not been beaten at Old Trafford now for 32 matches, since December 1994 when they lost to Forest.

Giggs's goal was the pick of United's four. A backheel from Cantona wrong-footed the Forest defence releasing Czech Karel Poborsky on the wing. His perfect cross was met by the Welshman with a thumping header.
Shearer and Cantona were not the day's only penalty scorers.
Chris Armstrong struck from the spot to give injury-hit Tottenham a 1-0 away win at Southampton, as did Croat Aljosa Asanovic in Derby's 1-0 win over Sunderland.
England's Nicky Barmby and Brazil's Juninho scored in open play as Middlesbrough came from behind to beat Everton, and in the London derby, Wimbledon beat West Ham 2-0.
Liverpool play Leicester on Sunday.
